_comment: COUPLING tier-2. `_PRECICE_BY_BACKEND` served 'CAN — proven by a real coupled run' for SEVEN backends under a header comment claiming every CAN came from a real two-participant coupling through OASiS's own orchestrator. Only TWO did: scikit-fem and FEniCSx, in `precice_can_verdicts_proven_by_a_real_run`, whose own docstring downgrades NGSolve and DUNE to the IMPORT GATE and is silent on the rest; deal.II, Kratos and SPARTA had no preCICE fixture at all, and no preCICE-linked C++ existed anywhere in the tree. This fixture supplies the four missing FEM coupled runs (SPARTA is a DSMC code with a different interface problem and its own load-order trap, so it has its own fixture). Each is a REAL two-participant preCICE coupling driven through the REGISTERED `couple_precice` tool, pairing the SAME scikit-fem DIRICHLET participant against that backend's NEUMANN participant, with non-matching interface meshes, serial-implicit sub-iteration, and the exchanged fields checked against a closed form computed here. The four differ in exactly the way the payloads claim they do: NGSolve shares the OASiS venv (and this run is where its two documented silent-wrong traps are actually avoided rather than only described); DUNE-fem lives in its own conda env and is reached through the PYTHONPATH recipe its payload prescribes, with both JIT schemes compiled BEFORE the Participant is constructed; deal.II has no Python API at all, so its participant is the shipped precice_heat_dealii.cc compiled here through CMake and checked with ldd to really link libprecice before it is run; Kratos needs its own interpreter AND a SUBSET shim, because the whole-site-packages recipe that works for DUNE shadows the good Kratos with the venv's broken wheel and breaks cyprecice's numpy ABI. Checking `converged` would not be a test: `couple_precice`'s own knowledge says `converged` is exit codes plus preCICE's per-window verdict and never looks at the values, and this fixture's mutation is exactly the case that proves the point.

_mutation.note: Flip the sign with which the SHARED scikit-fem Dirichlet participant EXPORTS the consistent nodal flux it computed — the one number the served FEniCSx pattern says the partner applies UNCHANGED. All four couplings go through this one participant, so all four are corrupted at once. Nothing the orchestrator reports changes: every participant still exits 0, preCICE still logs 'All converged', and each fixed-point iteration still converges (the Dirichlet-Neumann map's slope flips from -CL/CR to +CL/CR = +0.444, still inside the unit disc). Each converges to the WRONG fixed point — 284 K against a closed-form 306.15 K — and both sides then export the same sign of flux, so nothing is conserved across the interface. Every signal `couple_precice` returns stays green, which is why this fixture reads the exchanged values back out of the participants' own files instead of trusting the tool's verdict.
